claims.text: Calorimetry and DSC can determine HEA melting temperatures with uncertainties below 5%.
Calorimetry and DSC can determine HEA enthalpies of fusion with uncertainties below 5%.
Calorimetry and DSC can determine HEA entropies of fusion with uncertainties below 5%.
Calorimetry and DSC can determine the volume change of HEAs at melting with uncertainties below 5%.
Calorimetry and DSC can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of HEAs with uncertainties below 5%.
CoCrFeMnNi and AlCoCrFeNi are examples within the intended HEA composition range.
The proposed measurements use controlled heating rates and sample sizes.
The proposed operating window is a heating rate of 5–20 K/min and a sample mass of 10–50 mg under an inert atmosphere.
The method probes thermodynamic properties directly and therefore requires no structural mediator.
Thermal-energy absorption provides the mechanism for determining the proposed thermodynamic properties.
Phase-transformation kinetics contributes to the proposed measurement mechanism.
The approach may not apply to HEAs with complex phase transformations.
The approach may not apply when a 10–50 mg specimen is not representative of the alloy microstructure.
Measurement uncertainty may exceed 5% when the sample is not representative of the material microstructure.
XRD and TEM can serve as established comparison methods for validating the accuracy of the proposed melting-temperature, fusion-property, and melting-volume measurements.
Failure of calorimetry and DSC results to agree with comparison methods within the expected uncertainty would invalidate the approach.
